name: Cholar Dal
subtitle: bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp fresh, cut into small thin slivers

ingredients.note: cholar dal is meant to be faintly sweet

prepNotes: Rinse the chana dal in three changes of water, then soak 1 hour — it cooks more evenly and holds its shape.
Fry the coconut slivers in 1 tbsp of the ghee until golden and keep them aside; they go in at the end so they stay crisp.
Have the whole spices measured into one small bowl — the tempering takes under a minute.

steps.text: Drain the soaked dal and pressure cook with 700ml water, the turmeric and half the salt for 2 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally.
steps.tip: You want the grains soft but still individually visible, not collapsed into a puree.

steps.text: Open the cooker and mash lightly against the side with a spoon — about a quarter of the dal, no more.
Keep it on low heat while you make the tempering.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan. Add the bay leaves, dried red chillies, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: The cardamom pods puffing up is your cue that the spices have given their oil.

steps.text: Add the cumin seeds and grated ginger and fry 20 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the whole tempering into the dal, stir, and simmer 8 minutes uncovered.
Add the sugar and raisins and cook another 3 minutes until the raisins plump.
Stir in the garam masala and most of the fried coconut. Check the salt.
steps.tip: Taste for the sugar-salt balance here — it should read sweet first, then savoury.

steps.text: Scatter the last of the coconut over the top and serve hot with luchi.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It thickens considerably; loosen with hot water and re-warm gently on the stove.
